chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
If the guest steals, his hand is not cut. But if the guest hosts another guest and he steals, then the guest of the guest has his hand cut.

key_terms.اَلضَّيْفُ: the guest; a person received and hosted in another's dwelling
key_terms.ضَيْفًا: a guest; one brought in and hosted
key_terms.ضَيْفُ اَلضَّيْفِ: the guest of the guest; a secondary guest brought by the original guest
key_terms.قُطِعَ: his hand is cut; the hadd punishment is applied
key_terms.لَمْ يُقْطَعْ: his hand is not cut; the hadd punishment is not applied

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a guest steals, or if the guest of a guest steals?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning theft in the context of hospitality and guest-status. It distinguishes between the original guest and a secondary guest, indicating that legal liability for the hadd punishment differs according to the nature of access and lodging.
